scope.reader: A strong eight-year-old independently reading a serious introductory physics lesson.
scope.summary: All three original readability findings are resolved in the bound D1533 candidate. The affected explanations remain scientifically sound and faithful to the supplied source text and current Chinese scientific qualifications. PASS is local to these changes and their saved-flow adjacency, not a new whole-lesson, source-page, portrait, or publication approval.
scope.priorPassHandling: The original source, science, textual figure-context, and flow conclusions were read for context. Unaffected material was not substantively re-reviewed. The original immutable REVISE report is not overwritten; this report records only the disposition of its three findings in the changed candidate.

science.assessment: Charge is now linked to observable pushing and pulling, current to a flow of charge with an overall direction, and the electric and magnetic parts of a field to their effects on charged particles. Saying that the magnetic part can change the motion of a moving charged particle is appropriately qualified and does not assert that every moving particle is deflected or gains speed. The wave sentence identifies a traveling change in the electric and magnetic parts, rather than treating a field as a fluid, a contact-only force, or a picture. Field energy and momentum remain explicitly retained.

fidelity.assessment: These are explanatory glosses of the existing charge/current/field scope and the existing identification of light as an electromagnetic wave. The bold scope statement changes propagation to travel without changing its subject. The adjacent orbital free-fall, continuing gravity, bodily-effect, and hypothetical-removal qualifications are unchanged. Source references, source text, printed page, and empty numeric-change metadata are unchanged.

readability.assessment: The reader can now distinguish what charge lets objects do, what flows in a current, what a field can do to a charged particle, and what changes and travels in a wave. The short successive paragraphs supply concrete meaning before the later wave explanation uses it. The original circular definition and unexplained disturbance wording are gone.

sectionBreaks.assessment: The updated /section_breaks/1/after exactly matches current paragraph 10. Charge, current, field effects, and field energy remain together before the first section boundary; the light/wave paragraph stays after the existing weak-interaction footnote. No section boundary splits the new definitions.

science.assessment: The nucleus is correctly introduced as the small central part of an atom. Protons are positively charged and neutrons have no net electric charge; the latter introductory wording does not imply an absence of internal structure or all electromagnetic properties. Usually neutrons avoids asserting that every nucleus contains a neutron. Nucleons is introduced after its constituent particle names. Strong-interaction binding and electromagnetic proton repulsion both remain, and quantum laws still qualify the explanation of atomic structures, bonds, and material properties.

fidelity.assessment: The added nucleus and particle gloss explains the already-present nuclear distinction without substituting electrical attraction for nuclear binding. Naming these structures and properties removes the ambiguous They while preserving the Chinese quantum-law qualification. The existing scale, gravity, electrical-neutrality, short-range, and weak-decay qualifications are unchanged. Source references, source text, printed page, and empty numeric-change metadata are unchanged.

readability.assessment: The reader first learns where the nucleus is and the charges of its particles, then receives the collective name nucleons and the explanation of binding versus proton repulsion. These particles refers directly to the immediately preceding protons and neutrons. The explicit structures and properties referent removes the original pronoun ambiguity without expanding this overview into a separate quantum-physics lesson.

sectionBreaks.assessment: The nucleus/charge paragraph 15 is immediately followed by the nucleon/binding paragraph 16 and the quantum-qualified paragraph 17. No section break separates this explanatory chain. Existing surrounding anchors resolve at paragraphs 14 and 20 after the paragraph-count change.

science.assessment: The passage now separates the early rubbed-amber observation, Maxwell's theoretical inclusion of magnetic effects of changing electric fields, his wave prediction, later experimental support, and later radio technology. Maxwell is not credited with experimentally demonstrating waves or solely inventing radio. The steam-engine and early-electric-motor comparisons still distinguish experimentally established electromagnetic laws from Maxwell's complete field theory; they do not require all electrical devices to postdate that theory.

fidelity.assessment: The same source historical people and identity are retained literally: British physicist J. C. Maxwell and A. C. Popov. The second half of the nineteenth century and the multiple-researcher/engineering qualification remain. Later experimental support makes explicit the already-passed distinction between theory and experiment without introducing another named researcher or date. Source references, source text, printed page, historical-entity metadata, and empty numeric-change metadata are unchanged.

readability.assessment: Direct statements and adjacent short paragraphs now make the observation, theorist, prediction, later experimental confirmation, and technological use separately traceable. Much later and Later experiments establish the intended chronology. Steam engines and early motors no longer share one compressed comparison sentence. The remaining motor/radio contrast follows those separate examples, so a strong young reader can follow the argument without reconstructing the old from/to or one-way-sequence construction.

sectionBreaks.assessment: The revised /section_breaks/4/after exactly matches paragraph 22, and /section_breaks/5/before exactly matches paragraph 27. Paragraphs 22 through 27 remain in one section, keeping the amber observation, Maxwell theory/prediction, Popov qualification, and technology-order comparisons together. The next section starts at paragraph 28 with the unchanged applications paragraph.
